title:
Clean code.
Dangerous code.
body: 70% of this codebase was AI-generated. The vulnerabilities were human-readable.
label: AI-GENERATED
cta: Would you ship this without a human review?

title:
The patch window
is already closed.
body: Exploitation is landing before fixes are available.
label: DAYS TO EXPLOIT
cta: Can your team respond before the CVE drops?

title:
Security reviews
feel like a lecture.
body: The problem is not the review. It is when security enters the room.
cta: Where does your dev-security gap begin?

title:
The breach
starts at the lock.
body: Broken authentication remains the most common API failure pattern.
label: API BREACHES
cta: When did you last test your API auth?

title:
18 months of runway.
One breach cut it to 3.
body: The breach did not just expose data. It exposed the company’s future.
label: MONTHS OF RUNWAY
cta: Is security in your foundation or on your roadmap?

title:
Security belongs
before production.
body: A checklist after the breach is documentation. Controls before the code are prevention.
label: CONTROL POINTS
cta: Which gate is missing from your pipeline?

title:
20 minutes to find it.
3 years left open.
body: No exploit. No zero-day. A public bucket and a routine assessment.
label: TIME TO FIND
cta: What exists outside your official infrastructure?

title:
One checkbox.
A public cloud.
body: Misconfiguration is not dramatic. That is why it survives.
label: OF CLOUD BREACHES
cta: How many misconfigured assets are in your cloud?

title:
Found this in
production.
body: A wildcard policy. Created during an outage. Still active two years later.
label: FULL ACCESS
cta: Is this in your AWS account?

title:
Your code is clean.
Your image is not.
body: A container is a stack. Scanning one layer does not secure the runtime.
label: CVEs IN BASE IMAGE
cta: Have you scanned the image—not just the code?

title:
Private network
≠ private data.
body: A private VPC controls one boundary. It does not make every service safe.
cta: What is actually private in your VPC?

title:
Where does your cloud
security actually stand?
body: The gap is not documentation. It is enforcement.
label: MATURITY LEVELS
cta: Which level is your organization really at?

title:
AI did not invent
our security gaps.
body: It made the old failures faster, cheaper, and easier to scale.
cta: Are we losing to AI—or to the same gaps?

title:
You cannot secure
what you cannot see.
body: An employee prompt can become a data-exposure path in seconds.
label: ADDED BREACH COST
cta: What AI tools are your employees using?

title:
None of the models
were safe by default.
body: The same prompts produced vulnerable code across every assistant tested.
label: VULNERABLE OUTPUT
cta: Are you reviewing AI-generated code?

title:
Prompts are
the new malware.
body: Trusted content becomes an instruction when the model processes it.
label: ORGANIZATIONS TARGETED
cta: Is your AI hardened against prompt injection?

title:
The old tells
do not work anymore.
body: Same company. Same employees. AI-crafted messages changed the result.
cta: Was the request expected—not just believable?

title:
Deploying AI?
Secure the pipeline.
body: The model is only one part of the attack surface.
label: SECURITY GATES
cta: How many of these controls do you have?

title:
Activity is not
risk reduction.
body: A completed pentest is not the same thing as a remediated finding.
label: ACTIVITY / OUTCOME
cta: Are you measuring security or compliance?

title:
Your identity
is the perimeter.
body: Credential theft is industrialized—and session tokens can bypass MFA.
label: CREDENTIALS STOLEN
cta: Are your credentials in the next dataset?

title:
3 senior engineers missed it.
1 intern found it.
body: Expertise brings context. Fresh eyes bring questions.
label: MISSED / FOUND
cta: When did you last get fresh eyes on your code?

title:
Your response window
is smaller than a meeting.
body: From initial access to lateral movement, the clock is already running.
label: MINUTES AVERAGE
cta: Can your team respond inside the breakout window?

title:
Annual snapshots
miss continuous risk.
body: Pentests still matter. They cannot be the only layer anymore.
cta: Is annual testing still enough on its own?

title:
MFA is important.
MFA alone is not security.
body: The control is only as strong as the routes around it.
label: COMPROMISED ACCOUNTS HAD MFA
cta: Is your MFA phishing-resistant?

title:
19 minutes to infect.
3 hours to discover.
body: A maintainer account became a distribution channel.
label: TO SPREAD
cta: Could your build pipeline detect this?

title:
Prepare for the
next attack surface.
body: The future is uncertain. The signals are not.
cta: What are you preparing for now?

title:
The same five flaws
keep showing up.
body: The work is not glamorous. The basics still win.
label: CODEBASES / SAME FIVE
cta: Are these five findings in your codebase?

title:
Malicious packages
are accelerating.
body: The dependency graph is becoming an attack distribution system.
label: YEAR OVER YEAR
cta: Are you scanning dependencies beyond direct imports?

title:
The breach is not
the explosion.
body: It is the 241 days of access before anyone knows it is there.
label: DAYS TO IDENTIFY + CONTAIN
cta: Would you know if you were breached today?

title:
Zero Trust is
not a
product.
body: It is how access is designed, verified, limited, and continuously re-checked.
cta: Are you buying Zero Trust—or building it?
